newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Garbage piles up at environmental summit.
newsitem.headline: Garbage piles up at environmental summit.

text.p: More than 170 nations are meeting in New York this week to discuss how to save the planet from environmental disaster, but critics say the "Earth Summit" is itself a local ecological nightmare.
"For an agency that does nothing but preach, you see very little compliance," said Pranay Gupte, editor of The Earth Times, a newspaper that reports on the environment.

The New York Post newspaper said the meeting will produce 10 tons of garbage a day during the week-long meeting, called to discuss what has been done to save the planet since the first Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.

The New York Post reported that during Monday's first session, soda cans were thrown out with the regular garbage, white paper and other refuse was discarded into bins marked for newspapers only and offices were flooded with documents.
The fleet of limousines that ferry the thousands of diplomats and other participants around New York are also fouling the city's air and causing traffic gridlock.
The official drivers leave their engines idling in the United Nations driveway to keep air conditioners running in New York's stifling heat, the Post said.
